name: DDD Tactical Patterns
tagline: Encapsulating atomic business invariants inside small Aggregate Roots, immutable Value Objects, optimistic locking, and Outbox-backed Domain Events.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of Tactical DDD—from Entities and Value Objects to Aggregate sizing, `@Version` optimistic locking, and CQRS read bypass.

spark.summary: Building-block patterns—Entities, Value Objects, Aggregates, Domain Events, and Repositories—that encapsulate business invariants inside clear transactional consistency boundaries.
spark.keyTakeaway: Design small Aggregates around true atomic invariants, reference other Aggregates by ID rather than object graph, and coordinate cross-Aggregate side effects via Domain Events.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** Tactical DDD organizes domain code around **consistency boundaries** rather than database tables: **Value Objects** (`Money`, `DateRange`): Immutable, self-validating, compared by attributes.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Aggregate Root Optimistic Locking + Transactional Outbox Commit (ConfirmOrderCmd -> Order Aggregate (v4) -> orders (version=5) -> outbox_events); Order Aggregate Root Lifecycle & Optimistic Lock Guard (DRAFT (v4) -> CONFIRMED (v5) -> LOCK CONFLICT).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Balance transactional immediacy against optimistic-lock contention and service coupling. Keep Domain Services stateless and reserved only for operations spanning multiple Aggregates (`CurrencyConverter`).

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore how Transactional Outbox CDC, CQRS, and SOLID Aggregate design work together in production.

learningJourney.title: What are Tactical DDD Building Blocks
learningJourney.explanation:
Tactical DDD organizes domain code around **consistency boundaries** rather than database tables:

- **Value Objects** (`Money`, `DateRange`): Immutable, self-validating, compared by attributes.
- **Entities** (`Order`, `OrderLine`): Carry a continuous identity (`OrderId`) across state mutations.
- **Aggregate Root**: Controls all external access to a cluster of entities/value objects that *must* change together atomically, enforcing invariants on intention-revealing methods (`order.confirm()`) instead of public setters.
- **Repository & Domain Events**: Persist whole Aggregates atomically with optimistic locking (`version`) and emit past-tense events (`OrderConfirmed`) via an outbox.
learningJourney.purpose: The mechanism: understand how Tactical DDD Building Blocks works from first principles.

learningJourney.title: Why Anemic Models Fail Under Concurrency
learningJourney.explanation: In anemic domain models with `setBalance()`/`setStatus()` setters, business rules scatter across controllers and concurrent requests bypass invariants (e.g., two `POST /withdraw` requests both reading ₹1,000 and writing ₹200). Encapsulating invariants inside an Aggregate Root with a `version` CAS column makes invalid state transitions impossible to persist.

sectionDiagram.summary: Updating the Aggregate Root version and inserting the Domain Event into outbox_events in one ACID transaction eliminates dual-write drift.

ideas.title: Preventing Negative Wallet Balance via Aggregate + @Version
ideas.description: Replacing an anemic `Wallet.setBalance()` with `wallet.withdraw(Money)` and `@Version` optimistic locking caused the second concurrent withdrawal to fail cleanly with `OptimisticLockException`.

ideas.title: Immutable Money Value Object Catching Currency Bugs
ideas.description: Replacing raw `BigDecimal` + `String currency` across 14 services with `Money(amount, currency)` throwing `CurrencyMismatchException` on `add()` eliminated silent EUR+USD summation bugs.

learningJourney.purpose: The problem: see what breaks without Why Anemic Models Fail Under Concurrency under real concurrency or scale.

learningJourney.title: Where Tactical DDD Shines (and Where to Bypass Aggregates)
learningJourney.explanation: Reserve rich Aggregates for the write path of complex core domains; bypass them on read-only queries and batch ingestion.

comparison.choice: Use: Core State Machines & Concurrent Invariants
benefits: Order fulfillment, ledger postings, and seat holds become unit-testable in <1 ms with zero DB/HTTP mocks.
costs: Requires discipline around ORM mapping (no lazy-loaded `@OneToMany` proxies leaking outside).

benefits: Query denormalized SQL/DTO projections directly instead of hydrating full Aggregates.
costs: Read views updated via Outbox events are eventually consistent (~100 ms).

comparison.choice: Avoid: Simple CRUD Admin Tables & Batch ETL
benefits: Direct SQL or transaction scripts avoid needless hydration boilerplate.
costs: Hydrating millions of objects row-by-row destroys batch throughput.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: How to Size Aggregates & Coordinate via Domain Events
learningJourney.explanation: Follow Vaughn Vernon's rule: **design small Aggregates** around true atomic invariants (e.g., `Order` + `OrderLines` only—never put `Orders`, `Invoices`, and `Tickets` inside a `Customer` God Aggregate). Reference other Aggregates strictly by ID (`customerId: CustomerId`), modify one Aggregate per transaction, and use Domain Events + Outbox for cross-Aggregate rules.
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Small vs. Large Aggregates & Outbox vs. Sync RPC
learningJourney.explanation: Balance transactional immediacy against optimistic-lock contention and service coupling.

benefits: Minimal `OptimisticLockException` contention; decoupled side effects (email, loyalty).
Immediate ACID consistency across parent and all children.
costs: God Aggregate lock contention, slow hydration, and lazy-loading N+1 leaks.

benefits: Fastest to scaffold for simple CRUD.
costs: Validation logic duplicates across controllers and breaks under concurrent writes.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Architecture: Order Aggregate Lifecycle & Outbox
learningJourney.explanation: Keep Domain Services stateless and reserved only for operations spanning multiple Aggregates (`CurrencyConverter`). Enforce private setters on Aggregate Roots so every state transition emits its corresponding Domain Event into `outbox_events`.

sectionDiagram.title: Order Aggregate Root Lifecycle & Optimistic Lock Guard
sectionDiagram.summary: Intention-revealing methods + version CAS guarantee no caller can bypass order invariants or lose concurrent updates.

knowledgeCheck.question: A `Customer` Aggregate embeds all `Orders`, `Invoices`, and `SupportTickets` in one JPA entity graph, causing frequent `OptimisticLockException` failures whenever billing and support update the same customer simultaneously. What is the fix?

options.text: Split `Customer`, `Order`, `Invoice`, and `Ticket` into separate small Aggregates that reference `customerId` by ID and coordinate via Domain Events
options.feedback: Correct: small Aggregates aligned to true atomic invariants eliminate God Aggregate lock contention.

options.text: Remove the `@Version` optimistic lock column so all updates overwrite each other
Switch all collections to `@OneToMany(fetch = LAZY)` inside domain methods
options.feedback: Lazy loading leaks persistence concerns into the domain and causes N+1 queries or `LazyInitializationException`.
